questions.question: Let $f_{k}(x)=\frac{1}{k}\left(\sin ^{k} x+\cos ^{k} x\right)$ for $\mathrm{k}=1,2,3, \ldots$ Then for all $\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R},$ the value of $f_{4}(x)-f_{6}(x)$ is equal to :
questions.explanation:
$f_{k}(x)=\frac{1}{k}\left(\sin ^{k} x+\cos ^{k} x\right) f_{4}(x)=\frac{1}{4}\left[\sin ^{4} x+\cos ^{4} x\right] =\frac{1}{4}\left[\left(\sin ^{2} x+\cos ^{2} x\right)^{2}-\frac{(\sin 2 x)^{2}}{2}\right] =\frac{1}{4}\left[1-\frac{(\sin 2 x)^{2}}{2}\right] f_{6}(x)=\frac{1}{6}\left[\sin ^{6} x+\cos ^{6} x\right] =\frac{1}{6}\left[\left(\sin ^{2} x+\left(\cos ^{2} x\right)-\frac{3}{4}\left(\sin ^{2} x\right)^{2}\right]\right. =\frac{1}{6}\left[1-\frac{3}{4}(\sin 2 x)^{2}\right]$

Now $f_{4}(x)-f_{(6)}(x)=\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{6}-\frac{(\sin 2 x)^{2}}{8}+\frac{1}{8}(\sin 2 x)^{2} =\frac{1}{12}$

questions.question: If $\tan 15 ^\circ + \frac{1}{\tan 75 ^\circ } + \frac{1}{\tan 105 ^\circ } + \tan 195 ^\circ = 2a$, then the value of $\left(a + \frac{1}{a}\right)$ is :
questions.explanation:
Given:

$2a = \tan 15 ^\circ + \frac{1}{\tan 75 ^\circ } + \frac{1}{\tan 105 ^\circ } + \tan 195 ^\circ \implies 2a = \tan 15 ^\circ + \frac{1}{\tan \left(90 ^\circ - 15 ^\circ \right)} + \frac{1}{\tan \left(90 ^\circ + 15 ^\circ \right)} + \tan \left(180 ^\circ + 15 ^\circ \right) \implies 2a = \tan 15 ^\circ + \frac{1}{\cot 15 ^\circ } - \frac{1}{\cot 15 ^\circ } + \tan 15 ^\circ \implies 2a = 2\tan 15 ^\circ \implies a = \tan 15 ^\circ \implies a = \tan \left(45 ^\circ - 30 ^\circ \right) \implies a = \frac{1 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} \implies a = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

So,

$a + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1} + \frac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1} \implies a + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{{\left(\sqrt{3} - 1\right)}^{2} + {\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)}^{2}}{2} \implies a + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{8}{2} = 4$

questions.question: If $\sin x+\sin ^2 x=1, x \in\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, then $\left(\cos ^{12} x+\tan ^{12} x\right)+3\left(\cos ^{10} x+\tan ^{10} x+\cos ^8 x+\tan ^8 x\right)+\left(\cos ^6 x+\tan ^6 x\right)$ is equal to :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \sin x+\sin ^2 x=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \sin x=\cos ^2 x \Rightarrow \tan x=\cos x \end{aligned} \therefore$ Given expression $\begin{aligned} & =2 \cos ^{12} x+6\left[\cos ^{10} x+\cos ^8 x\right]+2 \cos ^6 x \\ & =2\left[\sin ^6 x+3 \sin ^5 x+3 \sin ^4 x+\sin ^3 x\right] \\ & =2 \sin ^3 x\left[(\sin x+1)^3\right] \\ & =2\left[\sin ^2 x+\sin x\right]^3 \\ & =2 \end{aligned}$ `

questions.question: If $15{\sin }^{4}\alpha + 10{\cos }^{4}\alpha = 6,$ for some $\alpha \in R,$ then the value of $27{\sec }^{6}\alpha + 8{cosec}^{6}\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.explanation: $15{\sin }^{4}\alpha + 10{\cos }^{4}\alpha = 6 15{\sin }^{4}\alpha + 10{\cos }^{4}\alpha = 6{\left({\sin }^{2}\alpha + {\cos }^{2}\alpha \right)}^{2} {\left(3{\sin }^{2}\alpha - 2{\cos }^{2}\alpha \right)}^{2} = 0 ∴3{\sin }^{2}\alpha - 2{\cos }^{2}\alpha = 0 {\tan }^{2}\alpha = \frac{2}{3} & {\cot }^{2}\alpha = \frac{3}{2} \implies 27{\sec }^{6}\alpha + 8{cosec}^{6}\alpha = 27{\left({\sec }^{2}\alpha \right)}^{3} + 8{\left({cosec}^{2}\alpha \right)}^{3} = 27{\left(1 + {\tan }^{2}\alpha \right)}^{3} + 8{\left(1 + {\cot }^{2}\alpha \right)}^{3} = 27{\left(1 + \frac{2}{3}\right)}^{3} + 8{\left(1 + \frac{3}{2}\right)}^{3} = 250$

questions.question: For any $\theta \in \left(\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{\pi }{2}\right),$ the expression $3{\left(\sin \theta - \cos \theta \right)}^{4} + 6{\left(\sin \theta + \cos \theta \right)}^{2} + 4{sin}^{6}\theta$ equals:
questions.explanation: $3{\left(\sin \theta - \cos \theta \right)}^{4} + 6{\left(\cos \theta + \sin \theta \right)}^{2} + 4{sin}^{6}\theta = 3{\left({\left(\sin \theta - \cos \theta \right)}^{2}\right)}^{2} + 6{\left(cos\theta + sin\theta \right)}^{2} + 4{sin}^{6}\theta = 3{\left({cos}^{2}\theta + {sin}^{2}\theta - 2sin\theta cos\theta \right)}^{2} + 6\left({cos}^{2}\theta + {sin}^{2}\theta + 2sin\theta cos\theta \right) + 4{sin}^{6}\theta = 3{\left(1 - 2sin\theta cos\theta \right)}^{2} + 6\left(1 + 2sin\theta cos\theta \right) + 4{sin}^{6}\theta = 3\left(1 - 4sin\theta cos\theta + 4{sin}^{2}\theta {cos}^{2}\theta \right) + 6\left(1 + 2sin\theta cos\theta \right) + 4{sin}^{6}\theta = 9 + 12{sin}^{2}\theta {cos}^{2}\theta + 4{sin}^{6}\theta = 9 + 12\left(1 - {cos}^{2}\theta \right){cos}^{2}\theta + 4{\left(1 - {cos}^{2}\theta \right)}^{3} = 9 + 12{cos}^{2}\theta - 12{cos}^{4}\theta + 4\left(1 - 3{cos}^{2}\theta + 3{cos}^{4}\theta - {cos}^{6}\theta \right) = 13 - 4{cos}^{6}\theta$

We know that $\sin \theta \sin \left(60 - \theta \right)\sin \left(60 + \theta \right) = \frac{1}{4}\sin 3\theta$

Now given $16\sin 20 ^\circ \sin 40 ^\circ \sin 80 ^\circ$

Comparing with above formula $\theta = 20 ^\circ$

we get $16\sin 20 ^\circ \sin 40 ^\circ \sin 80 ^\circ = 16 \times \frac{1}{4} \times \sin \left(3 \times 20 ^\circ \right) = 16 \times \frac{1}{4} \times \sin 60 ^\circ = 4 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2\sqrt{3}$

questions.explanation:
$\frac{1}{\sin \frac{\pi}{6}} \sum_{r=1}^{13} \frac{\sin \left[\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{r \pi}{6}\right)-\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-(r-1) \frac{\pi}{6}\right]}{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}+(r-1) \frac{\pi}{6}\right) \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{r \pi}{6}\right)} \begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\sin \frac{\pi}{6}} \sum_{\mathrm{r}=1}^{13}\left(\cot \left(\frac{\pi}{4}+(\mathrm{r}-1) \frac{\pi}{6}\right)-\cot \left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\mathrm{r} \pi}{6}\right)\right) \\ & =2 \sqrt{3}-2=\alpha \sqrt{3}+\mathrm{b} \end{aligned}$

So $a^2+b^2=8$

questions.question: The value of $sin10 ^\circ sin30 ^\circ sin50 ^\circ sin70 ^\circ$ is:
questions.explanation:
$\sin 10 ^\circ \sin 30 ^\circ \sin 50 ^\circ \sin 70 ^\circ = \sin 10 ^\circ \times \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 2\sin 50 ^\circ \sin 70 ^\circ \right) = \frac{1}{4}\sin 10 ^\circ \left(2\sin 50 ^\circ \sin 70 ^\circ \right)$

Using $2\sin A\sin B = \cos \left(A - B\right) - \cos \left(A + B\right) = \frac{1}{4}\sin 10 ^\circ \left(\cos 20 ^\circ - \cos 120 ^\circ \right) = \frac{1}{4}\sin 10 ^\circ \left(\cos 20 ^\circ - \cos \left(90 ^\circ + 30 ^\circ \right)\right) = \frac{1}{4}\sin 10 ^\circ \left(\cos 20 ^\circ + \sin 30 ^\circ \right) = \frac{1}{4}\sin 10 ^\circ \left(\cos 20 ^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{8}\left(2\sin 10 ^\circ \cos 20 ^\circ + \sin 10 ^\circ \right)$

Again, using $2\sin A\cos B = \sin \left(A + B\right) - \sin \left(A - B\right) = \frac{1}{8}\left(\sin 30 ^\circ - \sin 10 ^\circ + \sin 10 ^\circ \right) = \frac{1}{8}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{16}.$

questions.explanation: $\implies 2\sin \left(\frac{\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{2\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{3\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{5\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{6\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{7\pi }{8}\right) \implies 2\sin \left(\frac{\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{2\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\frac{3\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\pi - \frac{3\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\pi - \frac{2\pi }{8}\right)\sin \left(\pi - \frac{\pi }{8}\right) \implies 2{\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8}{\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{2\pi }{8}\right){\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{3\pi }{8}\right) \implies 2{\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8}{\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{2\pi }{8}\right){\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{3\pi }{8}\right) \implies 2{\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8}{\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right){\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{3\pi }{8}\right) \implies {\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8}{\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{3\pi }{8}\right) \implies {\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8}{\sin }^{2}\left(\frac{\pi }{2} - \frac{\pi }{8}\right) \implies {\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8}{\cos }^{2}\frac{\pi }{8} \implies \frac{1}{4}{\left(2\sin \frac{\pi }{8}\cos \frac{\pi }{8}\right)}^{2} \frac{1}{4}{\sin }^{2}\frac{\pi }{4} = \frac{1}{8}$

questions.question: The value of $2\sin \frac{\pi }{22}\sin \frac{3\pi }{22}\sin \frac{5\pi }{22}\sin \frac{7\pi }{22}\sin \frac{9\pi }{22}$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Given, $2\sin \frac{\pi }{22}\sin \frac{3\pi }{22}\sin \frac{5\pi }{22}\sin \frac{7\pi }{22}\sin \frac{9\pi }{22}$

Now by we know that $\sin \left(\theta \right) = \cos \left(\frac{\pi }{2} - \theta \right)$, so by using this we get $\sin \frac{\pi }{22} = \cos \left(\frac{\pi }{2} - \frac{\pi }{22}\right) = \cos \frac{5\pi }{11}$ and similarly $\sin \frac{3\pi }{22} = \cos \frac{4\pi }{11},\sin \frac{5\pi }{22} = \cos \frac{3\pi }{11},\sin \frac{7\pi }{22} = \frac{2\pi }{11},\sin \frac{9\pi }{22} = \cos \frac{\pi }{11}$

So, $2\sin \frac{\pi }{22}\sin \frac{3\pi }{22}\sin \frac{5\pi }{22}\sin \frac{7\pi }{22}\sin \frac{9\pi }{22} = 2\cos \frac{5\pi }{11}\cos \frac{4\pi }{11}\cos \frac{3\pi }{11}\cos \frac{2\pi }{11}\cos \frac{1\pi }{11} = 2\cos \frac{1\pi }{11}\cos \frac{2\pi }{11}\cos \frac{4\pi }{11}\cos \frac{8\pi }{11}\cos \frac{16\pi }{11}$

{As $\cos \frac{3\pi }{22} = - \cos \left(\pi - \frac{3\pi }{11}\right) = - \cos \frac{8\pi }{11}$ and $\cos \frac{5\pi }{11} = - \cos \frac{16\pi }{11}$}

$= \frac{2\sin \frac{\pi }{11}}{2\sin \frac{\pi }{11}}\cos \frac{\pi }{11}\cos \frac{2\pi }{11}\cos \frac{4\pi }{11}\cos \frac{8\pi }{11}\cos \frac{16\pi }{11} = \frac{2\sin \frac{4\pi }{11}\cos \frac{4\pi }{11}\cos \frac{8\pi }{11}\cos \frac{16\pi }{11}}{{2}^{2}\sin \frac{\pi }{11}} = \frac{2\sin \frac{8\pi }{11}\cos \frac{8\pi }{11}\cos \frac{16\pi }{11}}{{2}^{3}\sin \frac{\pi }{11}} = \frac{2\sin \frac{16\pi }{11}\cos \frac{16\pi }{11}}{{2}^{4}\sin \frac{\pi }{11}} = \frac{\sin \frac{32\pi }{11}}{{2}^{4}\sin \frac{\pi }{11}} = \frac{1}{16}\frac{\sin \left(3\pi −\frac{\pi }{11}\right)}{\sin \frac{\pi }{11}} = \frac{1}{16}$

questions.explanation:
We need to find the value of

$36\left(4{\cos }^{2}{9}^{∘} - 1\right)\left(4{\cos }^{2}{27}^{∘} - 1\right)\left(4{\cos }^{2}{81}^{∘} - 1\right)\left(4{\cos }^{2}{243}^{∘} - 1\right) = 36\left(\left(4{\cos }^{2}{9}^{∘} - 1\right)\left(4{\sin }^{2}{9}^{∘} - 1\right)\left(4{\cos }^{2}{27}^{∘} - 1\right)\left(4{\sin }^{2}{27}^{∘} - 1\right)\right) = 36\left(\left(4{\left(2\cos {9}^{∘}\sin 9 ^\circ \right)}^{2} - 4{\cos }^{2}9 ^\circ - 4{\sin }^{2}9 ^\circ + 1\right)\left(4{\left(2\sin {27}^{∘}\cos 9 ^\circ \right)}^{2} - 4{\cos }^{2}27 ^\circ - 4{\sin }^{2}27 ^\circ + 1\right)\right) = 36\left(\left(4{\sin }^{2}{18}^{∘} - 4 + 1\right)\left(4{\sin }^{2}{54}^{∘} - 4 + 1\right)\right) = 36\left(\left(4{\sin }^{2}{18}^{∘} - 3\right)\left(4{\sin }^{2}{54}^{∘} - 3\right)\right) = 36\left(\left(\frac{{\left(\sqrt{5} - 1\right)}^{2}}{4} - 3\right)\left(\frac{{\left(\sqrt{5} + 1\right)}^{2}}{4} - 3\right)\right) = 36\left(\left(\frac{\left(6 - 2\sqrt{5} - 12\right)}{4}\frac{\left(6 + 2\sqrt{5} - 12\right)}{4}\right)\right) = - 36\left(\left(\frac{{\left(2\sqrt{5}\right)}^{2} - 36}{16}\right)\right) = 36$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.question: The maximum value of $3\cos ⁡\theta + 5\sin ⁡\left(\theta - \frac{\pi }{6}\right)$ for any real value of $\theta$ is :
questions.explanation:
Given $f\left(\theta \right) = 3\cos ⁡\theta + 5\sin ⁡\left(\theta - \frac{\pi }{6}\right) \implies f\left(\theta \right) = 3\cos ⁡\theta + 5\left(\sin ⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \cos ⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{2}\right) \implies f\left(\theta \right) = \frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin ⁡\theta + \frac{1}{2}\cos ⁡\theta$

Now using the concept $a\cos x + b\sin x + c \in \left(c - \sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}},c + \sqrt{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}\right)$, we can write

Maximum value of $f\left(\theta \right)$ is $\sqrt{{\left(\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{75}{4} + \frac{1}{4}} = \sqrt{19}$

questions.question: Let $|\cos \theta \cos (60-\theta) \cos (60+\theta)| \leq \frac{1}{8}, \theta \epsilon[0,2 \pi]$. Then, the sum of all $\theta \epsilon[0,2 \pi]$, where $\cos 3 \theta$ attains its maximum value, is :
questions.explanation:
We know that
$(\cos \theta)\left(\cos( 6 0 ^ { \circ } - \theta ) \left(\cos \left(60^{\circ}+\theta\right)=\frac{1}{4} \cos 3 \theta\right.\right.$
So equation reduces to $\left|\frac{1}{4} \cos 3 \theta\right| \leq \frac{1}{8}$
$\begin{aligned}
& $\Rightarrow$|$\cos$ 3 $\theta$| $\leq \frac{1}{2}$ \\
& $\Rightarrow - \frac{1}{2} \leq \cos$ 3 $\theta \leq \frac{1}{2}$
\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow$ maximum value of $\cos 3 \theta=\frac{1}{2}$, here
$\begin{aligned}
& $\Rightarrow$ 3 $\theta$=2 $\mathrm{n} \pi$ \pm $\frac{\pi}{3}$ \\
& $\theta = \frac${2 $\mathrm{n} \pi$}{3} \pm $\frac{\pi}{9}$
\end{aligned}$
As $\theta \in[0,2 \pi]$ possible values are
$\theta=\left\{\frac{\pi}{9}, \frac{5 \pi}{9}, \frac{7 \pi}{9}, \frac{11 \pi}{9}, \frac{13 \pi}{9}, \frac{17 \pi}{9}\right\}$
Whose sum is
$\frac{\pi}{9}+\frac{5 \pi}{9}+\frac{7 \pi}{9}+\frac{11 \pi}{9}+\frac{13 \pi}{9}+\frac{17 \pi}{9}=\frac{54 \pi}{9}=6 \pi$

questions.question: If the value of $\frac{3 \cos 36^{\circ}+5 \sin 18^{\circ}}{5 \cos 36^{\circ}-3 \sin 18^{\circ}}$ is $\frac{a \sqrt{5}-b}{c}$, where $a, b, c$ are natural numbers and $\operatorname{gcd}(a, c)=1$, then $a+b+c$ is equal to :
questions.explanation: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\frac{3(\sqrt{5}+1)}{4}+5\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\right)}{5\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}\right)-3\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\right)}=\frac{8 \sqrt{5}-2}{2 \sqrt{5}+8} \\ & =\frac{4 \sqrt{5}-1}{\sqrt{5}+4} \times \frac{\sqrt{5}-4}{\sqrt{5}-4}\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & =\frac{20-16 \sqrt{5}-\sqrt{5}+4}{-11} \\ & =\frac{17 \sqrt{5}-24}{11} \Rightarrow a=17, b=27, c=11 \\ & a+b+c=52\end{aligned}$ .

questions.question: $\alpha = \sin 36 ^\circ$ is a root of which of the following equation
questions.explanation:
We know $\sin 36 ^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{10 - 2\sqrt{5}}}{4}$

Let $x = \frac{\sqrt{10 - 2\sqrt{5}}}{4}$

On squaring both sides, we get

${\left(4x\right)}^{2} = 10 - 2\sqrt{5} \implies 16{x}^{2} = 10 - 2\sqrt{5}$

Again squaring, we get

${\left(\sqrt{5}\right)}^{2} = {\left(5 - 8{x}^{2}\right)}^{2} \implies 5 = 25 + 64{x}^{4} - 80{x}^{2} \implies 16{x}^{4} - 20{x}^{2} + 5 = 0$

,

questions.question: $96\cos \frac{\pi }{33}\cos \frac{2\pi }{33}\cos \frac{4\pi }{33}\cos \frac{8\pi }{33}\cos \frac{16\pi }{33}$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given,

Expression $96 \cdot \cos \frac{\pi }{33} \cdot \cos \frac{2\pi }{33} \cdot \cos \frac{4\pi }{33}.........\cos \frac{16\pi }{33}$

Now we know that,

$\cos A \cdot \cos 2A \cdot \cos {2}^{2}A \cdot \cos {2}^{3}A..... \cdot \cos {2}^{n - 1}A = \frac{\sin {2}^{n}A}{{2}^{n}\sin A}$

Now using the above formula in given expression we get,

$96 \cdot \cos \frac{\pi }{33} \cdot \cos \frac{2\pi }{33} \cdot \cos \frac{4\pi }{33}.........\cos \frac{16\pi }{33} = 96 \times \frac{\sin \frac{32\pi }{33}}{{2}^{5}\sin \frac{\pi }{33}} = 96 \times \frac{\sin \left(\pi - \frac{\pi }{33}\right)}{{2}^{5}\sin \frac{\pi }{33}} = 96 \times \frac{\sin \left(\frac{\pi }{33}\right)}{{2}^{5}\sin \frac{\pi }{33}}\left(\text{as}\sin \left(\pi - \alpha \right) = \sin \alpha \right) = 96 \times \frac{1}{32} = 3$

questions.question: The value of $\cos ⁡\frac{\pi }{{2}^{2}}⋅\cos ⁡\frac{\pi }{{2}^{3}}⋅ \dots ⋅\cos ⁡\frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}}⋅\sin ⁡\frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}}$ is:
questions.explanation:
Given $cos\frac{\pi }{{2}^{2}} \cdot cos\frac{\pi }{{2}^{3}} \cdot ... \cdot cos\frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}} \cdot sin\frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}} = \frac{\sin \left({2}^{9}.\frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}}\right)}{{2}^{9}.\sin \frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}}}.\sin \frac{\pi }{{2}^{10}} \left(\mathrm{Using}\cos A.\cos 2A.\cos {2}^{2}A.\cos {2}^{3}A.\cos {2}^{4}A.....\cos {2}^{n - 1}A = \frac{\sin {2}^{n}A}{{2}^{n}\sin A}\right) = \frac{1}{{2}^{9}} = \frac{1}{512}$
